Spot builder

Pick the checklists in your break, set how many spots you want, and it splits the letters into the most even spots it can. Heavy letters get cut into two-letter ranges (SA-SH, SI-SZ) or Men and Women when that evens things out.

1. Boxes in the break

Add "| W" for women and "| auto" for autograph names. Pasted names count as one box.

2. Spots

Letters works for any checklist. Teams works for checklists with team names (football, basketball, baseball, college).
Best balance mixes strong and weak teams so every spot is worth about the same. Set the spot count to the number of teams for one team per spot (pick your team).
Players shown only with a college team. Anyone who also has a pro team in your boxes goes to that team.
Best balance mixes light letters together (like Q/V/Z). A to Z keeps neighbors together (like E-F).
Simple keeps whole letters wherever it can. Most even cuts more letters to get every spot closer to the same size.

3. Letter rule

A leading "The" is always skipped, so The Rock is R.

4. What counts more

Points per appearance, per box. A name in the base set and an auto set scores base plus auto.
Card makers put their stars and top rookies in far more autograph and insert sets than role players. Normal and Strong give a player more points the more hit sets they're in, so teams and letters with valuable players weigh (and cost) more.
Use this for the names buyers actually chase, so their letters get treated as the heavy hitters they are. One huge star can't be split, so their spot may stay a bit heavier. In team breaks you can star a whole team too, like "Yankees | 2".
How the points work, with examples

5. Pricing (optional)

Enter what the break costs you and it prices every spot by its share of the points, so the spot with the heavy hitters costs more.
Other costs: shipping, supplies, giveaways. Fees: your platform's selling and payment fees as a share of sales. Profit: what you want to make on top of your cost.
A sales goal skips the math above and prices spots to add up to that number.

Checklist library

Every checklist the builder knows about. New ones get added as they come in; each is one plain text file in the site's build folder.

How it works

1. Score every name

  • Each name earns points for every box it can come out of: base, autograph, insert, multi-person card.
  • Two boxes of the same product count twice.
  • Star multipliers scale a name up, so a Cena letter outweighs a letter full of NXT rookies.

2. Split the heavy letters

  • A fair share is the total score divided by your spot count.
  • Any letter above about 1.3 fair shares gets cut, either by second letter (SA-SH, SI-SZ) or into Men and Women, whichever evens it out better.
  • It keeps cutting until there are enough pieces to fill every spot.

3. Pack the spots

  • Best balance: biggest pieces go first into the lightest spot, then it swaps pieces between the heaviest and lightest spots until nothing improves.
  • A to Z order: finds the cut points along the alphabet that land closest to a fair share each.

4. Price it (optional)

  • Enter what you need the break to bring in, and each spot is priced by its share of the total score, rounded to the dollar.
  • Treat it as a starting point. Hype, rookies and case hits move real prices.

What counts more: how a name gets its points

Every name gets a point total. The builder adds those totals up by letter, then splits the letters so each spot ends up with about the same number of points. The four boxes in "What counts more" decide how many points each kind of card is worth, and star names let you say who buyers really want.

Default values: Base 1, Auto 2, Insert 0.5, Multi 0.5. A name earns every kind it appears in.

2. Player value: deeper players count more

Topps and Panini put their stars and top rookies in far more autograph and insert sets than role players. The "Player value" setting turns that into points: the more different hit sets a player is in, the more their auto and insert points grow.

Drake Maye, 2026 Flagship Football: in 6 autograph sets and 26 insert sets.
Off: auto counts once, 2 points. Normal: 2 x the square root of 6 = 4.9 points. Strong: 2 x 6 to the 0.8 = 8.4 points.

A role player in one autograph set gets the plain 2 points either way. Parallels of the same set don't count extra; only different sets do. Normal is the default.

3. More boxes, more points

Points are per box. Two boxes of a product double every name in it; names in two different products add together.

4. Star names multiply

Type a name, a bar and a number, like "John Cena | 5". The star multiplies that name's total after everything else. No number means 3.

3.5 x 5 = 17.5 points, so the C letters get heavier and the builder hands C fewer other names to even it out.

Partial names work: "Cena" matches John Cena and "Rhodes" matches "The American Nightmare" Cody Rhodes (3 letters minimum). One person can't be split across spots, so a very big multiplier can leave that one spot a little heavy; the page warns you when it does.

A heavier C letter gets split sooner (CA-CH, CI-CZ) or shares a spot with fewer letters, so the Cena spot isn't also stacked with other strong names.

6. Pricing from what you paid

Section 5 turns your cost into spot prices. Every spot is priced by its share of the points, so a spot holding the heavy hitters costs more.

Cost: 4 boxes at $275 = $1,100
Break even after 10% fees: $1,100 / 0.90 = $1,223
Target with 20% profit: $1,100 x 1.20 / 0.90 = $1,467
Spot with 8%
$117
Spot with 4%
$59

A lowest spot price keeps light spots from going out too cheap; the difference comes off the heavier spots so the total still hits the target. A sales goal skips the cost math and prices to that number.

7. Team breaks

Switch "Split spots by" to Teams. Each team gets the points of its players, so a team loaded with stars (or one you star, like "Yankees | 2") costs more.

  • Fewer spots than teams: teams are grouped so every spot is worth about the same (a strong team rides with a couple of light ones).
  • One spot per team: set spots to the team count for a pick-your-team break; each team is priced by its weight.
  • By division: for one league (NFL, NBA or MLB) the spots follow the divisions.
  • College / NIL players: anyone with a pro team goes to that team. College-only players can be their own spot, be split by the first letter of their first or last name (each letter goes to one of the lighter spots, and the spot shows "+ college A, K, T"), or be left out.
  • Old franchises roll into today's team: Oilers to Titans, Redskins to Commanders, SuperSonics to Thunder, Expos to Nationals.

8. Quick settings

  • Hits drive the price (high-end, auto-heavy boxes): raise Auto to 3 or 4.
  • Buyers want base sets (flagship, retail-style breaks): lower Auto toward 1.
  • Inserts are the chase (case hits like Cosmic Dust or Kaboom): raise Insert to 1 or 2.
  • Ignore something completely: set its box to 0.
  • A few names everyone asks about: add 3 to 5 of them as stars, usually at 3 to 5.

The score is only as good as the checklist and your star list. Breakers still make the final call on nicknames, multi-person cards and anything the checklist misses.
